<reason>B won a competitive debate by making the motion’s default-vs-concern line easier to vote: always-on message monitoring is intimate search, not living-room oversight; tracking often records harm rather than preventing it; and treating every “I’m at Sarah’s” as untrustworthy turns childhood itself into the exception that swallows the rule. A landed the strongest timing attack—B’s ordinary signs often arrive after first harm—but never fully answered the diary-scale problem, the help-seeking lifeline, or why legal minority alone justifies both tools as household default.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s conversion of A’s “a map is a check” into overinclusion: if no ordinary claim can be trusted without always-on tools, every teen is already a “specific concern,” so the motion’s exception becomes a standing search rule.</best_rebuttal>
